what: Every figure the public ai-systems repo publishes about this factory, with the command that derives it. Consumers run the derivation; they do not copy the value. A number handed over in prose is stale the moment main moves, and main moves several times a day.

not_sites: tools/diagram-compiler/diagrams_04_06.py — text(RX, 218, "classifyRouteBack", ...): a y-COORDINATE that happens to equal the figure. Excluded by hand by skill-ecosystem-00 and recorded here so nobody re-derives the exclusion.
demos/03-routeback/fixtures/cross-family-replay.jsonl — a recorded judge calibration sample. A replay fixture is EVIDENCE OF A PAST RUN and is never edited to match today's corpus.
figures.note: Two of the sites below are HISTORY, not live claims, and a redraw must leave them alone: docs/evidence.md section 5 and build_pdf.py's change table both record "152, contested -> 218, audited", which is what that revision settled. Two more are PINNED to a commit ("counts at factory 5739a97"), and a figure stated as-of a commit does not go stale when main moves — it is the correct way to publish a churning number, and the rest of the corpus would be better off copying it.

figures.note: COMPARE ELEMENT-WISE. level0_hubs held at 13 across the drift while TWO radii were wrong (positions 4 and 8): the set was stable, the members were the same thirteen skills, and only the numbers behind them moved. A stable count is not evidence of a stable array. Regenerate with npx tsx scripts/skill-ref-count.ts BEFORE reading. The Level-0 register only checks a hub is NAMED in CLAUDE.md, never that the count beside it is right (proposal cue-002), so a stale count here is exactly the failure that is not gated.
